summary: Compares two C++ type descriptors (a1 and a2) and returns 0 (no match) or 1 (match). Reads the type-name pointer at this+0x4, and when the descriptor is non-empty compares the name strings at +8 via sub_58FB90 (returning 0 if they differ), then applies qualifier-flag checks against bit masks in the leading bytes of a1/a2 and the match-flag dword a3.

local_names.a1: left type descriptor whose fields are read through this-relative bases
local_names.a2: right type descriptor being matched against
local_names.a3: match-flag dword selecting required qualifier bits
local_names.v3: type-name descriptor pointer read from a1+0x4
local_names.v4: type-name descriptor pointer read from a2+0x4

operations.description: v3 = *(a1+4) reads the type-name descriptor pointer at this+0x4; result is initialized to 1
Matching proceeds only when the type-name pointer at this+0x4 is non-null AND the byte at +8 of the pointed-to descriptor is non-zero; otherwise the default result (1) is returned
v4 = *(a2+4) reads the right-hand type-name descriptor pointer
When the two descriptor pointers differ, call sub_58FB90 on the name strings at +8 of each; a non-zero result (names differ) causes an immediate return of 0
Qualifier checks on the leading byte flags: return 0 if (a2&2) set while (a1&8) clear, or (a3&1) set while (a1&1) clear, or (a3&2) set while (a1&2) clear
Return the result (1) when all checks pass; the function is called by sub_5934E1 as part of descriptor/catch matching

unresolved: The exact meaning of the qualifier bits (2/1/8 in the leading descriptor bytes and 1/2 in a3) is inferred as const/volatile-style qualifier compatibility, not documented in the packet
The concrete layout of the type-descriptor structure behind this+0x4 is not evidenced beyond the +8 name-data offset
